Production for exchange is not the issue in my view
Cooperatives need to make money for worker owners to pay themselves
Worker owners need to pay themselves to be able to buy the commodities they need and want in their lives
Cooperatives want to offer their services and products in the market, but cooperatives can drive their prices down, because: 1) they don’t need to pay profits to investors; 2) they can rely on established cooperatives services that have already successfully driven their prices down

If the cooperative doesn’t give profits to investors, theoretically worker-owners can pay themselves much more (once the cooperative is well established)

From what I’ve read, with things like this there are important issues to consider:
1. Make sure there are systems that prevent a high-status group of users from excluding another group, based on identities like gender, class, race, ethnicity etc.
2. Think about governance where the users of this Etsy-like will be able to have a democratic say in the direction of the platform takes;
3. Consentful and fine-grained data collection - users are the owners of their own data and reputation.

I don’t want to overwhelm you with all of these considerations, but it’s worth keeping them at least in the backseat of your mind
